source_title: Run language-model agents in Minecraft with Mineflayer tools, persistent sessions and shell sandboxes. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Quickstart · Configuration · Tools · Teams · Bed Wars example
Point an LLM at a Minecraft server and give it something to do. It plays through Mineflayer , so it walks, mines, crafts, builds, fights and chats like a regular player. pi handles the model session. We've run Bed Wars matches with it, and a survival server with 50 agents on it at once.
Claude, GPT, Gemini, OpenRouter, or your own endpoint if it speaks the OpenAI Responses API
Sessions that survive restarts. Kill an agent, start it again under the same name, and it carries on
A shell for every agent (Docker, E2B or a plain local folder). Agents keep notes there and write little scripts that call their own game tools
Teams from a single JSON file, with DMs between agents and an optional shared machine
You'll need Node 22.19+, an API key for some model provider, and a Minecraft server. If you don't have a server, the repo comes with a dev one, which needs Java 21.
That's it. The default model is GPT-6.1 Terra, and Configuration covers the other providers and how to switch.
Join localhost:25565 from Minecraft 1.21.6 if you want to watch, and /tell Agent to talk to it. Its output and tool calls stream to the terminal. Ctrl+C stops it. Everything it knows lives in .agent-state/ / , so starting it again with the same name resumes the session.
Online-mode servers need --auth microsoft (you'll get a sign-in prompt). Agents assume survival; pass --game-mode if your server puts them in something else.
You get a Paper server on localhost:25565 and one agent. Change what it does with AGENT_OBJECTIVE in .env . State goes in the agent-state volume.
Already have a server? Just run the agent image:
Starts three agents who can message each other. Team config has the details. For something with rules and a referee, look at the Bed Wars example .
Flags, environment variables ( .env works) or a JSON file via --config . Flags win over env vars, env vars win over the file.
A heads-up about the shell: agents get one by default. That's E2B if E2B_API_KEY is set, otherwise Docker if it's running, otherwise a local folder, and local means commands run as you. Use --sandbox none if you'd rather they didn't have one.
